route: Bulgaria has no independent-means visa that I could confirm, and I could not read the official long-stay (type D) visa health-insurance rule: mfa.bg answers plain fetches with a Radware bot check and the Directorate Migration (mvr.bg) pages I reached say nothing on health cover. The statutory side is clear. Zakon za zdravnoto osiguryavane (ZZO) art. 33(1) point 3: 'Zadalzhitelno osigureni v Natsionalnata zdravnoosiguritelna kasa sa: ... chuzdite grazhdani ili litsata bez grazhdanstvo, na koito e razresheno dalgosrochno ili postoyanno prebivavane v Republika Balgariya'. So a couple holding long-term residence are compulsorily insured and must pay themselves if nothing else insures them.
policy: Art. 40(5) point 1 ZZO: people with no other insurance basis pay on an income 'ne po-malak ot polovinata ot minimalniya razmer na osigurit. dohod za samoosigurvashtite se litsa'. The contribution rate for 2026 is 8% (ZBNZOK 2026, art. 2). From 1 August 2026 the minimum income for self-insured people is EUR 620.20, so the base is EUR 310.10 and the contribution EUR 24.81 a person a month. Paid by the 25th of the next month; declaration form Obrazets No 7 to the NRA. Rights lapse if more than three monthly payments are missed in 36 months.
working: Since 1 Aug 2026: 620.20 / 2 = 310.10; x 8% = 24.808, rounded EUR 24.81 a person; x 2 = EUR 49.62 a month. Jan to Jul 2026: 550.66 / 2 = 275.33; x 8% = 22.03 a person; x 2 = EUR 44.05 a month (my arithmetic from the NRA minimum income of 550.66 reported by the same sources).

eu_citizen_difference: Not checked from a primary source. An EU citizen holding a right of residence normally keeps cover through EHIC or S1 from home, or falls in the same art. 40(5) group.
spot_check: Two sources agree on EUR 24.81 (the NRA release copy and the KiK-Info tables), but both are the same underlying NRA number. The law texts (ZZO art. 40(5), ZBNZOK art. 2) confirm the method: 8% x 310.10 = 24.81.
uncertainty: (1) Eligibility: ZZO art. 33(1)3 covers people with long-term or permanent residence permits. A new arrival on a D visa or first temporary permit may not be in the NHIF system yet and would then need private cover, which I did not price (no official D-visa wording and no tariff reached). (2) The EUR 620.20 minimum income comes from the state social insurance budget law, which I only saw via KiK-Info. (3) The amount rises with that minimum income each year. (4) Bulgaria joined the euro on 1 January 2026, so all figures are in euro.

statutory_must_pay.what: NHIF contribution for two people with no other insurance basis (8% x EUR 310.10 each, from 1 Aug 2026); compulsory for long-term or permanent residents. Same figure as the file's `amount`.

private_plan.insurer: DZI, Bulstrad, Euroins (named by the source; no insurer tariff reached)
private_plan.terms: Faster access to private specialists and hospitals on top of NHIF; Bulgaria-only; often age limits and pre-existing conditions excluded. Deductible and co-payments not stated by the source.
private_plan.pricing: Source's profile row 'Age 45, single or couple: EUR 50-80 individual' per month; midpoint EUR 65 x 2 people = EUR 130 a month. A broker's indicative range, not an insurer tariff. A second guide (Innovires) lists Bulstrad EUR 300-850 and Allianz Bulgaria EUR 400-1,200 with no column headers (probably annual); not used.
